questions.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Linear Equations and Inequalities
questions.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={n\in N:3n-5\le -4}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the natural numbers that satisfy the inequality $3n-5\le -4.$ 

So, we first need to solve our inequality for $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3n-5 & \le -4 \\ 3n & \le 1 \\ n & \le \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

However, no natural number satisfies the inequality above. So, we conclude that the set
$A$ contains no elements. Hence, $A=∅.$

questions.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={n\in Z:5n+25=10}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the integers that satisfy the equation $5n+25=10.$ 

So, we first need to solve our equation for $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5n+25 & =10 \\ 5n & =-15 \\ n & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

The solution is $n=-3,$ which is an integer.

Therefore, we can write the given set as

$$
A={-3}.
$$

questions.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={n\in N:2{n}^{2}-30<2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the natural numbers that satisfy the inequality $2{n}^{2}-30<2.$ 

So, we first need to solve our inequality for $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2{n}^{2}-30 & <2 \\ 2{n}^{2} & <32 \\ {n}^{2} & <16 \\ \sqrt{{n}^{2}} & <\sqrt{16} \\ |n| & <4 \\ -4<n & <4\end{aligned}
$$

The natural numbers that are solutions to the inequality above are $1,2,3.$ Therefore, the given set can be written as 

$$
A={1,2,3}.
$$

questions.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in {R}^{-}:3{x}^{2}\le 27}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the negative real numbers that satisfy the inequality $3{x}^{2}\le 27.$ 

So, we first need to solve our inequality for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2} & \le 27 \\ {x}^{2} & \le 9 \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}} & \le \sqrt{9} \\ |x| & \le 3 \\ -3\le x & \le 3\end{aligned}
$$

The negative real numbers that are solutions to the inequality above are $x\in [-3,0).$ Therefore, the given set can be written as 

$$
A=[-3,0).
$$

questions.problem: Which set is equivalent to $B={x\in R:{x}^{2}-5=0}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are real numbers that satisfy the equation ${x}^{2}-5=0.$

So, we first need to solve our equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-5 & =0 \\ {x}^{2} & =5 \\ x & =\pm \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=-\sqrt{5},\sqrt{5},$ and both of these solutions are real numbers.

Therefore, we can write the given set as

$$
B={\pm \sqrt{5}}.
$$

questions.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in R:3{x}^{2}+27=0}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the real numbers that satisfy the equation $3{x}^{2}+27=0.$ 

So, we first need to solve our equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+27 & =0 \\ 3{x}^{2} & =-27 \\ {x}^{2} & =-9 \\ x & =\pm \sqrt{-9} \\ x & =\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

However, since $x\in R$ and $\pm 3\text{i}\notin R,$ we conclude that the set $A$ contains no elements. Hence, $A=∅.$

$$
\begin{aligned}|n+6|<1 \\ -1<n+6<1 \\ -7<n<-5\end{aligned}
$$

The above inequality does not have natural solutions.

Therefore, the set $A$ is a null set:

$$
A=∅.
$$

questions.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in R:|x-3|=4}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the real numbers that satisfy the equation $|x-3|=4.$ So, we first need to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|x-3| & =4 \\ x-3 & =\pm 4 \\ x & =3\pm 4 \\ x & =-1,7\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=-1$ and $x=7,$ and both of these solutions are real numbers.

Therefore, we can write the given set as

$$
A={-1,7}.
$$

questions.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={k\in Z:|4k-2|\le 6}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the integer numbers that satisfy the inequality $|4k-2|\le 6.$ So, we first need to solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|4k-2|\le 6 \\ -6\le 4k-2\le 6 \\ -4\le 4k\le 8 \\ -1\le k\le 2\end{aligned}
$$

The integer solutions of the above inequality are $-1,0,1,2.$ 

Therefore, the given set can be written as 

$$
A={0,\pm 1,2}.
$$

questions.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in R:|2x+5|=13}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the real numbers that satisfy the equation $|2x+5|=13.$ So, we first need to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|2x+5| & =13 \\ 2x+5 & =\pm 13 \\ 2x & =-5\pm 13 \\ x & =\frac{-5\pm 13}{2} \\ x & =-9,4\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=-9$ and $x=4,$ and both of these solutions are real numbers.

Therefore, we can write the given set as

$$
A={-9,4}.
$$

$$

The solutions are $q=-3$ and $q=3,$ and both of these solutions are rational numbers.

Therefore, we can write the given set as

$$
A={-3,3}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Trigonometric Equations
questions.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in R\,:\,\operatorname{tan}⁡(4x)=0}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the solutions to the equation

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡(4x)=0
$$

 are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & =n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{n\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

where $n\in Z.$ 

Substituting different values of $n,$ we see that the solutions are

$$
x=0,\,\pm \frac{\pi }{4},\,\pm \frac{\pi }{2},\,\pm \frac{3\pi }{4},\,\pm \pi ,\,…
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ is equivalent to 

$$
A={0,\,\pm \frac{\pi }{4},\,\pm \frac{\pi }{2},\,\pm \frac{3\pi }{4},\,\pm \pi ,\,…}.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the solutions to the equation

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)=1
$$

are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\pi x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+2n\pi  \\ \pi x & =\pi (\frac{1}{2}+2n) \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}+2n\end{aligned}
$$

where $n\in Z.$ 

Substituting different values of $n,$ we see that the solutions are

$$
x=…,-\frac{7}{2},-\frac{3}{2},\frac{1}{2},\frac{5}{2},\frac{9}{2},…
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ is equivalent to 

$$
A={…,-\frac{7}{2},-\frac{3}{2},\frac{1}{2},\frac{5}{2},\frac{9}{2},…}.
$$

canonical_examples.problem: List the elements of the set $A = \{n \in \mathbb{N}: 5n - 2 \leq 21 \}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the natural numbers that satisfy the inequality $5n - 2 \leq 21.$ 

So, we first need to solve our inequality for $n{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}5n-2 & \le 21 \\ 5n & \le 23 \\ n & \le \frac{23}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

The positive integer solutions of the inequality above are $1,2,3,4.$ Therefore, the given set can be written as 

$$
A = \{1,2,3,4\}.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Quadratic Equations and Inequalities
canonical_examples.problem: List the elements of the set $A = \{x \in \mathbb{Z}: x^2 - 9 \lt 0\}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the integers that satisfy the inequality $x^2 - 9 < 0.$

So, we first need to solve our inequality for $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-9 & <0 \\ {x}^{2} & <9 \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}} & <\sqrt{9} \\ |x| & <3 \\ -3<x & <3\end{aligned}
$$

The integer solutions of the inequality above are $0,\pm1,\pm2.$ Therefore, the given set can be written as 

$$
A = \{ 0, \pm 1, \pm 2\}.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Absolute Value Equations and Inequalities
canonical_examples.problem: List the elements of the set $A=\{k \in \mathbb{Z}: |k-1| \leq 4 \}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the integers that satisfy the inequality $|k-1| \leq 4.$ So, we first need to solve for $k{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}|k-1|\le 4 \\ -4\le k-1\le 4 \\ -3\le k\le 5\end{aligned}
$$

The integer solutions of the above inequality are $-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3,4,5.$ 

Therefore, the given set can be written as 

$$
A = \{0,\pm1,\pm2,\pm3,4,5 \}.
$$

canonical_examples.problem: List the elements of the set $A = \left\{ x\in \mathbb R \: :\:  \tan \left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right) = 0  \right\}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Notice that the solutions to the equation

$$
\tan \left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right) = 0
$$

 are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi x}{2} & =n\pi  \\ x & =2n\end{aligned}
$$

where $n\in\mathbb Z.$ 

Substituting different values of $n,$ we see that the solutions are

$$
x = 0,\, \pm 2 ,\, \pm 4,\, \pm 6,\, \ldots
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ is equivalent to 

$$
A= \{0,\, \pm 2 ,\, \pm 4,\, \pm 6,\, \ldots\}.
$$
